item.statement: Cauchy-Schwarz + Parseval + 1-Lipschitz variance bound give the ReLU single-neuron budget

chk.evidence:
The Fourier + Cauchy-Schwarz single-neuron template comes from Morwani et al. ICLR 2024 (arXiv 2311.07568v2; I read the full PDF).
- App. F.1, "Proofs for cyclic groups (Theorem 7)", bounds a quadratic neuron in three steps: "By Plancherel's theorem, the norm constraint is equivalent to ...", then Cauchy-Schwarz (and AM-GM), giving sqrt(2/27)/(p^{1/2}(p-1)).
- The same section says "E_c[w(c)] = 0, because shifting the mean of w does not affect the margin".
- Morwani treats ReLU only empirically (Fig 1a, Fig 4, the L2-regularised ReLU runs). There is no ReLU bound.

Gromov 2023 (arXiv 2301.02679; I grepped the full PDF) analyses quadratic activation. It says only "The weights (6)-(7) also work for other activation functions, including ReLU", which is an empirical claim with no bound.

Other papers checked:
- Li et al. AISTATS 2025 (2402.09469): power activations only.
- Memana 2026 (arXiv 2608.04451, single ReLU neuron): a dynamics counterexample to MAIS-O60, with no margin or budget bound.
- McCracken et al. 2505.18266: random-frequency constructions, with no single-neuron norm budget.

The step Var(f(X)) <= L^2 Var(X) for L-Lipschitz f is a textbook fact, proved in one line with an independent copy of X. It needs no citation.

I found no paper that bounds the ReLU single-neuron Fourier budget for modular-addition margins. So the ReLU extension (the 1-Lipschitz variance step on top of diagonal Parseval) is new as far as I found, but the template is Morwani's.

A possible technical issue: the text sums over j in F_p, but Var(h) does not control the j = 0 term h^(0) ~ E[h]. This should be justified, either by w^(0) = 0 (the mean of w is margin-irrelevant, as in Morwani F.1) or by summing over j != 0.

Searches run:
- "ReLU network modular addition maximum margin upper bound Fourier single neuron proof"
- "1-Lipschitz function variance contraction Var(f(X)) <= Var(X) lemma"

Notes are in /Users/ruhaanrajadhyaksha/projects/grok/heracles/paper/litcheck/items/t13-relu-budget/CHECK.md.

recommended_citations.why: App. F.1 (proof of Thm 7) is where the Plancherel + Cauchy-Schwarz single-neuron Fourier budget originates, for quadratic neurons. It also shows that the mean of w does not affect the margin, which justifies dropping the j=0 term. Cite it in the ReLU paragraph as the template being extended.
Optional. Its quadratic analytic solution reportedly also works for ReLU, but only empirically, with no bound. It supports the statement that no prior ReLU margin bound exists.

chk.recommended_change:
In appendix.tex, ReLU paragraph (l.283):
1. Change "Cauchy--Schwarz over j, Parseval for the diagonal coefficients, and Var(h)<=Var(sum_t u_t)" to "The Plancherel/Cauchy--Schwarz single-neuron argument of \citet[App.~F.1]{morwani2024feature}, extended to ReLU by the 1-Lipschitz variance bound Var(sigma(X))<=Var(X) (take an independent copy X': Var f(X)=\tfrac12\E(f(X)-f(X'))^2)".
2. Justify the j=0 term. Either sum over j in F_p\{0}, or add "w.l.o.g. \hat w(0)=0, since shifting the mean of w does not change the margin". The reason is that Var(h) does not bound \hat h(0,...,0).
